title: Self / other objects in time: event-owned clocks and consequential attention
summary: SelfAndOtherObjectsInTime turns the recent self/other and temporal-address discussion into a falsifiable mechanism line. The executable gates separate stable reference origin from resident history, bind actor/patient/perspective roles, make time event-relative, nest child events with writeback, admit interruptions by downstream consequence, actively probe hidden causal maps, and allocate temporal precision according to relevance. It does not claim a theory of consciousness or a literal neural circuit.

nodes.claim: Tests whether a continuing reference process can preserve self/other role structure across detours while time is owned by events, interruptions write back into resident state, and temporal precision is allocated to downstream consequence rather than raw magnitude.
nodes.survived: Across Gates 1–9, the narrow mechanisms that survive are: return changed-but-stable rather than reset or overwrite; distributed role binding; event-relative phase rather than a fixed wall clock; discovered event boundaries; nested parent/child local time with child writeback; consequence-based event admission; active causal probing under a matched budget; selective temporal precision; and online reallocation of timing bandwidth without resetting event identity.
nodes.killed: Snapshot reset, leaky anchor overwrite, role-blind and SELF/OTHER-only binding, a fixed absolute clock, whole-stream/fixed-window timing, flat parent/child time, no-writeback parenting, raw-magnitude salience, admit-all/ignore-all policies, random/no causal probing, uniform timing, fixed timing slots, one-step-lagged reallocation, and reset-on-reallocation all fail their matched gates. The repo still supplies software phase/consequence scaffolds and does not establish biological implementation or consciousness.

edges.why: SelfAndOtherObjectsInTime explicitly identifies the frequency-addressed operator-composition line as its address-plus-resident-state ancestor; the new gates add event-owned phase, event admission and dynamic timing bandwidth rather than claiming code inheritance.
The repo explicitly connects nested parent/child processing to FusionMachine's resident-computation idea: a parent remains present while a selected child runs and later writes back.

The repo explicitly connects perspective/event detours that leave residue to the Sigh residue line, while keeping the new claim narrower: residue becomes resident history that changes the resumed process.
Gate 7 explicitly reuses expected-information-gain experiment selection under an equal probe budget to discover which hidden causal map should govern future event admission.
The repo explicitly frames Gate 6/7 as the observability/write problem: which local perturbation survives transport into a downstream observable, then which intervention identifies that map.

SelfAndOtherObjectsInTime names the_whorl / ArtificialCortex as the substrate-level precursor for replacing a supplied phase coordinate with locally generated oscillatory or propagating field phase. This is a future bridge, not an implemented inheritance claim.

motifs.title: Time is owned by a continuing event, and its precision is a resource
motifs.description: The frequency-addressed/operator line supplies resident state and address; FusionMachine supplies persistent parent computation; AnotherOddThing/ReadWrite supply active identification and observability; SelfAndOtherObjectsInTime combines those motifs into event-local clocks whose bandwidth can change without resetting event identity.
